statement: Exact completion of the lift extension — The completion of $1\to\pi_0\to E\xrightarrow qG\to1$ is the exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow\widehat E\xrightarrow{\widehat q}G\longrightarrow1. \] It is the extension attached to the completed outer action. An invariant discretization therefore supplies a canonical comparison of extensions, with identity maps on $P$ and $G$.
notes: D.a; finite-index topology and the centre-free pullback give exact completion.

statement: Finite subgroups of completed surface orbifold groups, including reflections — Every finite subgroup of $\widehat E$ is conjugate to a finite subgroup of $E$. Two finite subgroups of $E$ conjugate in $\widehat E$ are conjugate in $E$. These finite subgroups are cyclic rotation groups or dihedral groups, with a single reflection included as the dihedral case of order two.
depends_on: D.1; B.1; Bridson--Conder--Reid Theorem5.1; Boggi--Zalesskii Theorem6.3
notes: D.a; includes all dihedral stabilizers through a characteristic prime-order rotation subgroup.

statement: The comparison of full and partial section classes — For every subgroup $H\leq G$, completion induces a bijection \[ \operatorname{Sec}(E_H\to H)/\pi_0 \ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Sec}(\widehat E_H\to H)/P, \qquad E_H=q^{-1}(H). \] Both sets are finite. In particular the first conjecture on scan 393 holds for geometrically realized actions, with orientation-reversing operators allowed.
notes: D.a; actual kernel-conjugacy, with quotient labels, for every full and partial section.

statement: The exact profinite fixed subgroup of a section — Let $s:H\to E_H$ be a nontrivial discrete section. Its fixed subgroup $P^{s(H)}=C_P(s(H))$ is trivial when $s(H)$ contains a nontrivial rotation. For a reflection $s(H)=\langle t\rangle$, it is $1$ for a noncompact real component and is the closure of the primitive oval subgroup, isomorphic to $\widehat\Z$, for a compact real component. The same assertions hold for every profinite section by D.3.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: 393: pi^G=1 question; orientation-positive insertion on391 is material
notes: D.a; nontrivial rotations give 1, reflection ovals give Zhat, reflection lines give 1.

statement: Unique maximal sections require a rotation — A finite subgroup of $\widehat E$ containing a nontrivial rotation is contained in a unique maximal finite subgroup. The assertion for every nontrivial finite subgroup is false, already for type $(0,3)$ with reflections.
notes: D.a; unique maximal overgroup holds for a subgroup containing a rotation; the type(0,3) reflection has two.

statement: A well-defined transfer of the geometric rotation invariant — For a realized $E$, its rotation invariant on finite-order elements transfers uniquely to the torsion of $\widehat E$ by conjugating each torsion element into $E$. This assertion uses the orientation module, so that conjugation by an orientation-reversing element acts by $-1$ on its values. Its values embed canonically in $\widehat T\otimes_{\Z}\Q/\Z$, where $\widehat T=T\otimes_{\Z}\widehat\Z$.
notes: D.a; orientation-aware transfer formula on every torsion element of the geometric completion.

statement: Equivariance of the profinite rotation invariant — Let $E$ be the lift group of a finite action on an orientable hyperbolic surface of finite type, and put $P=\widehat\pi\triangleleft\widehat E$. Every automorphism $\alpha$ of $\widehat E$ preserving $P$ and its indexed peripheral structure satisfies \[ \mu_{\widehat E}(\alpha(u))=\alpha_T\bigl(\mu_{\widehat E}(u)\bigr) \qquad (u\in\widehat E\text{ of finite order}). \] Here $\alpha_T$ is the induced automorphism of the orientation line $\widehat T$ defined in A.2, and $\mu_{\widehat E}$ is the invariant of D.6. The assertion holds for compact and noncompact surfaces, and for actions containing orientation-reversing elements.
notes: D.a; every punctured and closed geometric orbifold extension, including reflection-containing groups. Closed single-cone case handled by a characteristic cover.

statement: All finite subgroups in the geometric completion in the three requested types — Let $M=\Gamma_{g,\nu}$ include puncture permutations and orientation reversal. For $(g,\nu)=(0,3),(0,4),(1,1)$, completion induces a bijection on conjugacy classes of finite subgroups of $M$ and $\widehat M$. Every finite subgroup of $\widehat M$ is solvable. For every finite $K\leq M$, \[ N_{\widehat M}(K)=\overline{N_M(K)},\qquad C_{\widehat M}(K)=\overline{C_M(K)}. \] These assertions concern $\widehat M$ with its given embedding in $\Out_{\rm lac}(P)$.
depends_on: B.23; B.25; Ribes--Zalesskii Theorem2.6 and Corollary2.9; Bridson--Piwek Proposition5.10
notes: D.b; all finite subgroups of the geometric completions in types(0,3),(0,4),(1,1), including orientation reversal.

statement: The nonsolvable discrete possibilities in genus at most two — A nonsolvable finite subgroup of the extended mapping class group of a punctured orientable surface of genus at most two is realized on a sphere and has group $A_5$ or $A_5\times C_2$. Its puncture set is invariant under the corresponding icosahedral action. In particular it has at least twelve punctures. This classification does not assert the absence of additional nonsolvable finite subgroups in completions for all larger puncture numbers.
notes: D.b; the nonsolvable discrete possibilities in genus at most two are the sphere groups A5 and A5 times C2, requiring at least twelve punctures.

statement: Finite torsion in the odd-prime normalized pro-$p$ centralizer — Let $p$ be odd, let $F^{(p)}$ be the free pro-$p$ group on $x,y$, and define $GT_{0,p}$ by the normalized automorphisms \[ F_{\lambda,f}(x)=x^\lambda,\qquad F_{\lambda,f}(y)=f^{-1}y^\lambda f, \quad \lambda\in\Z_p^\times,\quad f\in(F^{(p)})', \] satisfying the two-cycle and three-cycle equations. Every finite subgroup of $GT_{0,p}$ is cyclic of order dividing $p-1$. There is a subgroup of order $p-1$, and every finite subgroup is conjugate in $GT_{0,p}$ to a subgroup of it. For $p\geq5$ this supplies finite loop-preserving outer automorphism groups which are not conjugate to geometric groups of the three-punctured sphere.
depends_on: A.7; Harbater--Schneps MainTheorem(a); elementary Magnus filtration
notes: D.b; complete odd-prime pro-p centralizer statement; p=5 gives nongeometric order four. Does not claim a full profinite lift.

statement: Executed finite checks and their exact scope — The program \texttt{code/root/finite\_checks.py} verifies the two-cycle and three-cycle equations in every Heisenberg group $H(\F_p)$ for $p=5,7,11$ and every $\lambda\in\F_p^\times$, using \[ f(a,b)=[a,b]^{(\lambda^2-1)/24},\qquad m=(\lambda-1)/2. \] In particular it verifies an order-four normalized automorphism at $(p,\lambda\bmod p)=(5,2)$ and an order-three one at $(7,2)$. The multipliers of the corresponding infinite finite-order subgroups are Teichm\"uller lifts of these residues; the integer $2\in\Z_5^\times$ itself has infinite order. D.10, not the finite checks alone, proves the existence of compatible infinite pro-$p$ lifts.
notes: D.b; exact finite Heisenberg certificates at p=5,7,11, with two-cycle and three-cycle equations, automorphism property and order.

D29 refutes the requested geometric recognition in type (0,4) by an actual peripheral involution. The geometric-completion assertions are proved in D8. Later claims settle the full finite subgroup abstract types and supply exact conjugator equations, without establishing existence of every required conjugator.

statement: Restriction and normal descent with the peripheral step included — For an open subgroup $V\leq P$, restriction of the corresponding finite covering defines an injective map \[ \operatorname{Discr}(P)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Discr}(V), \qquad\Delta\longmapsto\Delta\cap V. \] For normal $V$, its image consists exactly of the lattices $\Lambda\subset V$ whose outer deck action $P/V\to\Out_{\rm lac}(V)$ is induced by orientation-preserving loop automorphisms of $\Lambda$. The cyclic peripheral subgroups of the descended lattice have closures equal to the specified peripheral subgroups of $P$.
depends_on: A.7; A.12; C.17; D.1; Paris Theorems1.7,3.2

statement: The image for a nonnormal finite covering — Let $V\leq P$ be open, $W=\operatorname{core}_P(V)$ and $\Lambda\in\operatorname{Discr}(V)$. Set $\Lambda_W=\Lambda\cap W$. The image condition for $\Lambda$ is that the full deck action of $P/W$ on $W$ is induced by orientation-preserving loop automorphisms of $\Lambda_W$. This condition is independent of a choice of coset representatives. The unique extension is $N_P(\Lambda_W)$, and its intersection with $V$ is $\Lambda$.
notes: D.c; arbitrary open subgroup handled by its exact normal core and lattice intersection comparison.

statement: The explicit nonextending discretization in scan 354 — Let $U=\mathbf P^1-\{0,1,\infty\}$ and $U'=\mathbf P^1-\{0,\infty,1,-1\}$, with the double cover $z\mapsto z^2$. Put $P=\widehat{\pi_1(U)}$, let $V\triangleleft P$ be its index-two subgroup, and let $\Lambda=\pi_1(U')\subset V$ be the geometric discretization. There is an explicit continuous loop automorphism $\gamma$ of $V$ for which $\gamma(\Lambda)$ is a discretization of $V$ that does not extend to $P$, although it has the same prediscretization as $\Lambda$.

statement: A precise fixed-set formula for every actual action — Let $A$ be a group, $J\leq A$, and $G\leq A$ a finite subgroup. Under the left action of $G$ on $A/J$, \[ (A/J)^G=\{aJ:a^{-1}Ga\leq J\}. \] It is the disjoint union of the $C_A(G)$-orbits \[ \coprod_{[a]} C_A(G)\big/\bigl(aC_J(a^{-1}Ga)a^{-1}\bigr), \] where $[a]$ ranges over $J$-conjugacy classes of the labelled embeddings $g\mapsto a^{-1}ga$ occurring in $J$. This formula applies to actual discretizations with $(A,J)=(A(P),\Aut_{\rm lac}(\pi_0))$, to outer discretizations with $(A,J)=(B,M)$, and to prediscretizations with $(A,J)=(B,\overline M)$.
notes: D.c; actual, outer and prediscretization fixed sets with labelled-embedding orbits and exact stabilizers.

statement: Torsion-free extensions with an invariant discretization — Let $1\to P\to\mathcal E\to G\to1$ be a profinite extension with $G$ finite, $P=\widehat\pi_0$ hyperbolic, and the outer action preserving the loop structure and a discretization. A torsion-free $\mathcal E$ is the profinite completion of a torsion-free discrete surface group, with the descended peripheral system. The quotient surface may be nonorientable.

notes: D.d; full profinite extension recognized in the invariant-discretization case, with orientation-reversing quotient allowed.

statement: The unmarked pro-$p$ extension statement for punctured surfaces — A finitely generated torsion-free pro-$p$ group $\mathcal E$ containing an open free pro-$p$ group $P$ of rank $r$ is free pro-$p$. Its rank is \[ 1+\frac{r-1}{[\mathcal E:P]}. \] In particular the displayed quantity is an integer. This proves the underlying-group assertion for punctured pro-$p$ surfaces, without identifying the peripheral system. More generally, every torsion-free profinite group with an open normal pro-$p$ subgroup is itself pro-$p$. Thus D.19--D.20 apply to arbitrary finite-quotient extensions of their pro-$p$ kernels; the quotient is forced to be a $p$-group.
notes: D.d; free underlying pro-p group with exact Schreier rank, before peripheral recognition.

statement: Recognition of the peripheral pro-$p$ extension — Let $p$ be any prime, let $P$ be the pro-$p$ completion of an orientable hyperbolic surface group of type $(g,\nu)$ with $\nu>0$, and let \[ 1\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow\mathcal E\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow1 \] be an exact sequence of pro-$p$ groups with $G$ finite. Assume that $\mathcal E$ is torsion-free and its outer action preserves the $P$-conjugacy classes of the peripheral subgroups. Choose one $L_j$ from each $\mathcal E$-orbit of these classes. Then \[ \mathcal N_j=N_{\mathcal E}(L_j)=C_{\mathcal E}(L_j)\simeq\Z_p, \] and the pair $(\mathcal E;\{\mathcal N_j\})$ is continuously isomorphic, preserving the indexed peripheral conjugacy classes, to the pro-$p$ completion of a compact surface with its boundary circles. Its interior is orientable for odd $p$. At $p=2$ the interior may be nonorientable; its orientation character is the induced action on the orientation line of $P$.
depends_on: A.7; D.18; WilkesRelative Propositions5.9,5.11; WilkesClassification Theorem3.3

statement: Recognition of the closed pro-$p$ extension — Let $P$ be the pro-$p$ completion of a closed orientable surface group of genus $g\geq2$. A torsion-free pro-$p$ group $\mathcal E$ containing $P$ as an open normal subgroup is the pro-$p$ completion of a closed surface group. The surface is orientable at odd $p$. At $p=2$ a nonorientable surface is allowed, and its orientation character is the action on the orientation line of $P$.

We have not proved that every full profinite extension in D(d) is a completed surface pair.

statement: The two lifting conditions cut out exactly the multiplier-$1$ subgroup modulo $3$ — In $B=\Out_{\rm lac}(\widehat\pi_{0,3})$ let $S_3$ be the geometric positive subgroup. Its centralizer is $GT_0$, with the normalized description $(\lambda,f)$ of Harbater--Schneps. Every element of $GT_0$ has an automorphism representative commuting with the chosen order-two lift $\theta$. The elements with an automorphism representative commuting with the chosen order-three lift $\omega$ are exactly \[ GT_0^{(3)}=\{(\lambda,f)\in GT_0:\lambda\equiv1\pmod3\}. \] This subgroup has index two. The two representatives need not be the same representative; this is the two-condition formulation on scans 316--317.

statement: The arithmetic subgroup and the two fixed points — The intersection of the usual Galois image $G_{\Q}\to GT_0$ with $GT_0^{(3)}$ is the image of $G_{\Q(\sqrt{-3})}$. The order-three fixed points in $U=\mathbf P^1-\{0,1,\infty\}$ are $e^{\pm i\pi/3}$, and the order-two lift has one fixed point in $U$. Thus the requirement to fix the chosen order-three section is a proper finite-index restriction, even on the Galois subgroup.

statement: Normalizer, stabilizer, and the forced lift — Let $1\to\pi\to E\xrightarrow q\mathcal G\to1$ have centre-free kernel, and let $K\leq E$ be a finite subgroup on which $q$ is injective. Assume $C_\pi(K)=1$, as holds for a nontrivial rotation stabilizer in the anabelian geometric situation and its completion. Put $G_Q=q(K)$ and let $Q$ denote the $\pi$-conjugacy class of $K$. The restriction \[ q:N_E(K)\longrightarrow\mathcal G \] is injective and has image the stabilizer $\mathcal G_Q$ of $Q$. Its inverse on that image is a canonical homomorphism. In a two-group situation $\mathcal G=\Gamma G$ with $\Gamma$ centralizing $G$, its restriction gives the forced lift of $\Gamma_Q=\Gamma\cap\mathcal G_Q$, and this lift centralizes $K$.
notes: E.b; forced lift and normalizer image under the exact trivial-centralizer hypothesis; oval correction stated.

statement: Explicit discrete centralizers and pointwise kernels — For the three actions in the question, the full extended geometric groups, their centralizers, their normalizers, and their pointwise kernels on the exceptional points are as follows. Here $D_{2n}$ has order $2n$. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} (g,\nu),G&M&C_M(G)&N_M(G)&C_M(G)^{\natural}\\ \hline (0,3),S_3&S_3\times C_2&C_2&S_3\times C_2&1\\ (1,1),C_4&\mathrm{GL}_2(\Z)&C_4&D_8&C_2\\ (1,1),C_6&\mathrm{GL}_2(\Z)&C_6&D_{12}&1 \end{array} \] The last column fixes every exceptional point individually, not merely its orbit under $G$.
notes: E.b; exact discrete centralizers, normalizers, and kernels on critical points for S3,C4,C6.
E.b; arbitrary specified commuting group is not recovered from its pointwise kernel; exact intersection identity proved.

statement: LM4-F.a: fixed discretizations and prediscretizations — For $M=\Gamma_{g,\nu}$ and $H=\overline M\leq B$, the sets of outer discretizations and prediscretizations are $B/M$ and $B/H$. For a given finite $G\leq B$ their fixed sets are exactly D.16's transporter sets and centralizer-orbit decompositions. In the three types of D.8, every fixed prediscretization has a fixed outer discretization above it. The same lifting conclusion holds for a finite solvable $G$ and genus at most two for the orientation-preserving geometric group covered by Boggi's Theorem C. Over a fixed coset represented by $b$, the fibre is \[ (H/M)^{b^{-1}Gb}, \] with its full labelled-embedding decomposition as in D.16.
notes: F.a; stable label LM4-F.a. Transporter formula is unconditional; nonempty-fibre cases named precisely.

u}}}(G) =\overline{C_{\Gamma^+_{g,
u}}(G)}. \] The corresponding equality with the full loop-outer group in place of the geometric completion is false already for $(g,
u)=(0,3)$ and $G=S_3$.

statement: LM4-F.b, the intrinsic open-image statement — Let $M\leq B$ be an oriented geometric subgroup, $H=\overline M$, $N=N_B(H)$, and let $i:G\hookrightarrow H$ be a fixed finite embedding. Conjugation defines an action of $N/H$ on the set of $H$-conjugacy classes of embeddings $G\hookrightarrow H$. The image of the continuous homomorphism \[ C_N(i(G))\longrightarrow N/H \] is exactly the stabilizer of $[i]$, and its kernel is $C_H(i(G))$. When the orbit of $[i]$ is finite, this image is open. The orbit is finite for solvable finite $G$ in genus at most two and for every finite $G$ in the three low types of D.8.

statement: LM4-F.c: the exact canonical lift of a section stabilizer — Let $\pi$ be a centre-free discrete surface group or its full profinite completion, and put \[ A=\Aut_{\rm lac}(\pi),\qquad B=\Out_{\rm lac}(\pi). \] Let $G\leq B$ be finite and let $s:G\to A$ be a specified lift with $C_\pi(s(G))=1$. The natural map \[ C_A(s(G))\longrightarrow C_B(G) \] is injective. Its image is the stabilizer of the $\pi$-conjugacy class $[s]$ in the set of lifts of the labelled inclusion $G\hookrightarrow B$. Its inverse is the canonical homomorphism lifting that stabilizer to $A$ and centralizing $s(G)$. In the profinite case it is continuous. For geometrically realized actions with a nontrivial rotation the section-class set is finite, so this stabilizer has finite index and is open in the profinite case.

statement: The unrestricted uniqueness assertion for reflection ovals — For a reflection fixing an oval, the lifting map in F.4 has kernel $\Z$ in the discrete case and $\widehat\Z$ after completion. Consequently it is not injective and its lifts are not unique without further data.
